summary: Submitted draft/submission.json (action=check) with draft/check-plan.json and draft/check-harness.go for the accepted obligation c-adopted-term-never-regresses (unit unit-c-adopted-term-never-regresses). The check fixes one discriminator for the investigated premise: a heartbeat-shaped AppendEntries handled by Raft.processHeartbeat — the callback NewRaft registers through Transport.SetHeartbeatHandler — on a NetworkTransport connection goroutine, interleaved with a second, higher-term AppendEntries that the same node's main goroutine handles on a separate connection. The harness keeps the target's own NetworkTransport (including its isHeartbeat classification, its direct callback dispatch and msgpack framing) and only substitutes the StreamLayer with an in-process net.Pipe fabric, and it wraps the injected StableStore so that exactly one CurrentTerm write is held inside SetUint64, which parks the callback between its term decision and the term it publishes; the second request is deliberately not heartbeat-shaped so it must take the main-loop path. Semantics are unchanged: no term comparison, branch or write order in the target is altered, and no target file is modified. The plan's prerequisite is the node's own completion report for the higher-term request (term_advanced), and the property compares the term context observed afterwards (Raft.CurrentTerm) with the term the node reported adopting. I validated the exact submitted harness bytes locally in a fresh copy of the captured module: the test starts, exits 0 and emits admitted_term=6 while the observed context_term=5 and the durable CurrentTerm=5 (stored write sequence 0,1,1,5,6), reproducibly in 5/5 runs. So the planned observation will be a measured violation (a completed, fully observed assertion), not an exit-code oracle; the first assessment will record it as awaiting the checker-correspondence review, since execution_attribution is not applicable to a zero-exit run. Scope limits are recorded as explicit uncertainties: the equality encoding coincides with 'not lower than the admitted term' only because this prefix admits exactly two term writes, the TCP scheduling of the production deployment remains a source-level premise of the check, and the downstream vote consequence is not observed. Preflight with the trusted validator returned valid=true; no target code was executed for the submission itself.
